entries.x: Phase 100 (ST5, 2.33.0; design: STAPLES.md §8). Sara speaks the open Agent2Agent protocol, version 1.0 (specification, normative a2a.proto), written from the specification with no SDK. She works in two directions: Server. Other agents ask her things, within what you allow them. Client. She asks other agents. Everything is in Settings → Connections → Apps and services → Other agents. A2A is off until you switch on Let other agents reach her.

entries.x: Add an agent she can ask: paste its address or card URL. She fetches the card through src/net-guard.ts (SSRF rules apply; in private local mode only this computer, or your home network if you tick Allow agents on my network). SARA_A2A_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7860 SARA_A2A_KEY=<agent key> node scripts/a2a-conformance.ts checks a running server against the shapes the specification requires: the card fields the JSON-RPC envelope and error codes the version header a streamed message (every event one of task / message / statusUpdate / artifactUpdate) get, list paging, cancel, and subscribe on a terminal task the REST error shape Without a URL and key it skips with the reason.

entries.x: Sara's add-ons extend the existing harness rather than replacing its memory, safety, approvals or workspace controls. The website groups entries into Everyday Assistant, Research & Documents, Developer, Creator, Small Business, and Private & Local. Each is a guided checklist, not a bulk installer. entries.t: defineTool({ name, description, parameters, permission, cost, run })
entries.x: A tool she can use, registered in Sara as <id>__<name> (my_addon__greet). parameters is a small JSON schema (type, properties, required, enum); Sara checks the arguments before your code sees them. permission is ask (the default; the owner approves each call) or auto (capped at ask until the owner changes it in Settings → Tools). run(args, sara) returns text or { content, card }. cost is US dollars per call (or null: it costs money, the amount is unknown).

entries.x: A setting on the add-on's settings window: text, number, switch, choice or secret. Every setting needs a tip (10 to 260 characters) that says what it does. entries.x: Since 2.36.0 (Phase 103, staples ST8; design: STAPLES.md §11) Sara can keep plans of her own: follow-ups on things you tell her ("ask how the interview went on Friday evening") and goals you keep at together ("Run a 10k in April"). It is off by default, per companion, and everything she does on her own is listed, capped, budgeted and stoppable.

Planner → Her plans → Let her keep her own plans (the big switch at the top). The same switch turns everything off at once: a message she is writing right then is stopped and not sent, and her planned items stay listed as paused. Switch it on again and they come back (a time that passed while she was off moves to the same time on the next day). Clear her plans removes them. Household members have their own plans in their own space, off by default; the owner can't read them. The demo never has…

Follow-ups (code, no model). When you mention something coming up in one of your own chats ("the interview is on Friday", "I have a dentist appointment tomorrow", "the renewal window opens Dec 1"), she plans to ask how it went (that evening, 7 pm) or to remind you (that morning, 10 am). The chat shows Added to her plans under her reply. She can also add one with her agenda_add tool when she says "I'll ask you Friday how it went". Goals (proposal cards). For a big job that splits well — research several things at once, write it up, check it — she runs a team: helpers working at the same time, each with its own model, tools and budget, then one result and one approval point for anything that leaves Sara. (Microsoft Teams is TEAMS.md. Code work with a coder, tester and reviewer is the older team task; standing helpers on a schedule are crews.)

In any chat: "Get a team to compare three e-bikes under $2,000 and write it up as a Word document." She calls team_run, which only proposes a plan; a card appears in the chat. Or Team → Team runs: describe the job, pick the result (a message here, Word, PDF or Markdown), Plan it.

Part of the plan What you can change Helpers (roles) Name; kind: researcher, drafter, checker or your own role; model (Auto = your usual model for that kind of work); tools (✉ marks actions); budget (tokens, minutes, optional $); May use the computer. Parts Which helper, the title, and what each part waits for. Parts that wait for nothing run at the same time (up to 3). Result A message in the chat, or a document in your Library (make_document) with the sources listed. The budget for the whol…

Each helper's part shows live on the run and on its chat card: waiting, working, done, its tokens, the round; Pause (no new part starts; helpers stop before their next move), Go on, Stop. Scratchpad: researchers note each finding with its source (note_finding); every later helper sees the numbered findings, and drafts cite them as [n]. Checker: checks the draft against the findings and the receipts (claims of things done that no receipt backs, citations that point at no finding, and its own V…

Sending, posting, buying and computer actions are not done during the run: a helper's call is queued and it is told so. At the end one card lists every queued action (who asked, what it does). Untick any you don't want, then Do the ticked actions, or Do none. Each action is checked again against your current settings before it runs.

After a run finishes, Save as a team recipe (on the run in Team → Team runs) keeps the plan's shape under a name, e.g. Product comparison: Kept Never kept the helpers (kind, name, instructions), models (Auto unless you pinned one), tools, budgets, May use the computer findings, reports, receipts, queued actions, the log, the result the parts and what each waits for; the checker's rules (its instructions) the job text itself: it becomes {job} the result type (message, Word, PDF, Markdown) anyt…

In a private chat, or with Nothing leaves this computer on, helpers use models on this computer only (a cloud model in the plan falls back to Auto, which picks a local one) and tools that reach outside are left out.

Each run (plan, parts and their reports and receipts, scratchpad, checks, actions, log, tokens and cost) is a row in team_runs in your space, and a run record (kind team) like any team task. A run that was working when the server stopped shows interrupted by a restart; it doesn't restart by itself.
Owner only: household members, the demo and paired devices get 403. Route group team-runs is audited. At most two runs work at once.

The certificate chain is downloaded (cached until it expires), every certificate on the path must be inside its dates, the first must name echo-api.amazon.com in its subject alternative names, each must be signed by the next, and the path must en…

Sara's downloadable model is English (US) and also works for the other English locales (add the locale in the console → Language settings, paste the same model). For Spanish, French, German, Italian or Portuguese (Brazil): add that locale, paste the model and translate the sample phrases (keep the intent and slot names). She answers in the language you speak to her in.

"There was a problem with the requested skill's response": Sara refused the request. Her log says why (Alexa: refused a request (…)): usually a different skill id (paste it again) or private local mode. Alexa says the skill isn't available / no answer at all: the endpoint must be the public https://…/alexa address with a trusted certificate. Test it from the console's Test tab. "This Alexa isn't linked": make a code in Sara and say "link code …" within 10 minutes. She takes too long: see Time…

One switch per person: while it is on, Sara runs every command, desktop, browser and computer-use action she takes for you without an approval card, including the kinds that otherwise always ask (payments and purchases, account and security settings, saved logins, destructive commands, the browser's own settings pages, form-fill review cards, the plan check, advisory and ship-gate cards). Where: Settings → Connections → Computer use → Always allow everything (top of the page).

Pick how long: 1 hour, 1 day or Until I turn it off. Press Turn on… and read the one-time warning. Confirm it's you: your owner token, the current two-step code, or a passkey (the same step-up as making an API key). From a remote device the owner approves it first (new-device approval). On your computer, the Sara app (Windows or Mac) shows its own card once with Always allow everything: press it there. A phone can never relax what a computer allows; after that one press the computer asks noth…

She never types into password fields and never types text shaped like a key or a sign-in token (she hands those over with "your turn"). These are limits, not approvals. Hidden windows and tabs, banking and password managers stay off limits; administrator prompts are your click; the browser's own password, payment and sync pages stay blocked. Requests from other people still ask: other apps, outside requests, forwarded mail or messages, answers from a linked server, group chats. The switch cov…

The owner. Household adults only when the owner ticks May turn on Always allow everything on their card in Settings → Household. Taking it back turns theirs off at once. Never kids (kid-safe members), demo or off-the-record spaces, and never when an organization policy forbids Always allowed (pins.alwaysAllow: false).

The Android app (android/README.md) shows your server's web page, so every new screen since 3.1 (Messages, communities, errands, the Library, Settings 3,...) is in the app as soon as the server has it. The app itself only adds what a web page can't do on a phone. This page lists what the newer screens need from the app, what U2.9 added, and how to build and try it. Everything that runs on its own is in one place: Settings → You → Automations. You make an automation there or by asking Sara ("every Friday at 3, fill my time sheet from my calendar and send it to me"). The watches, event triggers, routines and repeating reminders you set up elsewhere are listed on the same page, each read and switched through its own page's store (nothing is moved).

A schedule: every day, every weekday, chosen days of the week, or a day of the month (the 31st is the last day in shorter months), at a time in your time zone (Settings → You → About you). Daylight-saving changes are handled: 3 PM stays 3 PM. An email arrives (optionally from a sender or with some words): the owner's mailbox, the same source as When this happens. In order: tell me (chat, and a phone or desktop notification unless you pick chat only), ask Sara (a task you wrote, run as an ordinary turn in the automation's own chat), draft an email, fill a document (one of your templates in the Library, through fill_document), run a recipe, add a bill or add an expense (the last three are written instructions to her, so the money and recipe tools keep their own approvals). Any current model from OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI works well for chat, coding and tools. The cheaper "mini", "flash" or small models are fine for background jobs. Sara ships with list prices for a few of them (checked on the providers' pricing pages on 2026-10-27; see COSTS.md), and the Usage and costs page lets you add your own. Cloud providers apply their own content rules whatever Sara's settings say: adult content usually needs a model on your own hardware or a provider that allows it.

With many steps (read ten files, look up five things, then write a summary), Sara normally calls one tool, waits for the result, calls the next, and so on: every call is a round trip to the model. Code mode lets her write one short script that makes all those calls and hands back only the result. It is faster, and it uses fewer tokens on big jobs. It is off by default. Turn it on in Settings → Skills & tools → Tools and approvals → Code mode: one script for many tool calls.

She is offered the run_code tool when a job needs many tool calls: in coding conversations, and in any chat once she has already made two tool calls in the same turn. Never in group chats or partner chats.

Every call inside a script goes through exactly the same checks as a call she makes directly: A tool set to Ask me first shows its normal approval card in the chat. The script waits (paused) until you answer. Deny makes that call fail inside the script; she sees "ToolDenied". A tool that is Off, not available in this chat, or limited by your admin's policy is refused. The safety check-up, the loop guard, plugins' checks, the sandbox try for commands, private conversations and Nothing leaves t…

In a separate Node process with Node's permission model: it can't read or write files, start programs, open network connections or look up names. The only way out is Sara's own tools. On Linux with bubblewrap it also runs inside bubblewrap; with the container sandbox (Settings → Tools → Isolation) inside a container with no network. On Windows without a container engine the fence is Node's permission model and network guard (a Node-level control, not an OS sandbox). Limits: 20 000 characters …

The policy (Settings → Household → Policy) has Turn off Code mode: then no one on the server can turn it on and run_code is never offered. You can also set the run_code tool itself to Ask me first or Off in Tools and approvals.

A computer you already have (a spare PC, a mini PC, a Mac): free apart from electricity. A VPS (rented server): Sara alone runs on a small one. Use at least 2 GB of memory and 20 GB of disk (see REQUIREMENTS.md). In late 2026 plans of that size from the common hosting companies typically cost somewhere around $5-20 a month; check the provider. A VPS with a GPU big enough for local models costs far more, often more than a cloud model or a subscription would for one person.

entries.x: Sara helps you decide; she doesn't decide for you. Ask her things like "Should I take the job in Denver?", "Which is better, the Civic or the Corolla?", "pros and cons of renting" or "compare these three phone plans".

Options and what matters. She gathers the options and the criteria that matter to you, each with a weight from 1 (matters a little) to 5 (matters most). If you didn't say what matters, she asks (at most two short questions). Scores, with where they came from. Each option gets a score per criterion: either your own 1–10 rating ("you said"), a fact with its source ("$24,000, from honda.com"), or her estimate, which is always flagged as "my estimate". She looks facts up instead of guessing; anyt…

Every decision is saved in your own space (a household member's decisions are theirs alone). When you pick, she records your choice and why; give her a date ("in 3 months") and the planner reminds you: "How did choosing X work out?". Tell her how it went (and rate it 1–5), and the next time you decide something similar she recalls "last time you chose …, and it went …". Ask her "what did I decide about …" or "list my decisions" to see them again.

"Compare" makes a plain table of items and their attributes (price, size, rating…) from the values she was given or found, with sources. Missing values are marked "—" and counted; nothing is filled in. For a weighted pick between them, she uses the decision helper.

Settings → Connections → Devices and sign-in → Approve new devices. When it is on, a sign-in with the owner token or a passkey from somewhere other than this computer waits for your OK. "Somewhere else" includes another computer or phone, and anything that comes through a tunnel or a proxy (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, Caddy, nginx), even though those connect from 127.0.0.1.

The new device shows a 5-character code, for example K7Q2M (no look-alike letters; any case). You get a prompt on a device you already use (and a push), and a message from her in Telegram or Discord if you linked them. The code is not in those messages: read it off the new device. Approve: type the code in the prompt, or reply approve K7Q2M to her in Telegram or Discord. Refuse: Deny, deny K7Q2M, or just deny (refuses every waiting request). No answer in 10 minutes is a no. A device can never…

On this computer none of these asks for the owner token: being signed in as the owner is enough.

Devices at most: over the limit, the device you used longest ago is signed out. API keys, Home Assistant and Sara's hands don't count. Any sign-in (browser, Sara app, an app approved with a code) unused for 30 days is signed out; one in use never is (since 3.49.1). When a device was signed out, its sign-in page says why: 30 days without use, or signed out under Devices and sign-in. Allowed addresses: the names this server answers to besides localhost and IP addresses (for example sara.example…

Ask Sara for a document and she makes a real file: a Word document (.docx), PDF, Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx), PowerPoint presentation (.pptx), Markdown, CSV or web page (.html). It works with every model, local or in the cloud, with nothing to install. "Make me a one-page PDF about the history of coffee." "Make a Word resume for Pat." "Put our monthly budget in a spreadsheet, with totals." "Turn these notes into five slides for the book club."

The file arrives as a card under her reply: Download saves the file. Open shows it: a PDF opens in your browser; Word, Excel, PowerPoint and the rest show a preview in a window (the preview is a picture of the content, not Office itself). Make changes puts "Change “…” (document #12):" in the message box. Say what to change and she makes version 2. Earlier versions are kept: Other versions on the card lists them. In Telegram, Discord and other chat apps you get the file itself.

Every document she makes is saved in your Library (it opens, searches and shares like anything else there). In an off-the-record chat it is kept for that chat only. Household members' documents are in their own space; nobody else sees them.

entries.t: Sara in your code editor (Zed, JetBrains and other ACP editors)
entries.x: Editors that speak the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) can use Sara as their coding agent: you chat with her in the editor's agent panel, she reads and edits the files of the folder you have open, runs commands in the editor's terminal, and asks you in the editor before she changes a file or runs a command. It is the same Sara as in the web app: her character, memory, approval rules and safety checks all apply. Sara speaks ACP protocol version 1 (schema release schema-v1.29.1, November 2026).

The page lists errands waiting on you first, with the question, an answer box when it needs one (a choice, an address, a note) and Approve step, Skip, Stop, Edit. Each errand's Timeline shows every step's result and its evidence: the tool's "Verified:" read-back, the reply's mail id, or "your word" for what you did yourself. She only says a step is done when it shows there. You get a notification when an errand needs you (not in quiet hours or private local mode).

Each person's errands live in their own space; a household member's are theirs alone. Errands can't be started from a private chat, and nothing runs while private local mode is on. The runner rides the reminder tick (no timer of its own).

errand_start (asks once; its card is the plan), errand_status (steps, evidence, what she needs), errand_list, errand_update (a note, facts, deadline, budget, add or remove a step), errand_stop. Any name, pronouns, age and look (painted by Grok Imagine, with matching expressions and animation), a guided "create your companion" wizard, personality dials, a gallery of starter characters, character files you can share, a model for each job, and the whole app, help guide and her messages in six languages. Give her PDFs (scans too, and books of 500 to 1,000 pages), Word, Excel, PowerPoint, e-books, web pages and notes. She learns the key points, answers from them and says which document and page it came from, with a link that opens it right there (LIBRARY.md).

entries.x: Say "Hey Sara" and talk, hands-free, in the Sara app for Windows, Mac or Android, or with sara wake on a Linux desktop. A small keyword model on the device listens only for her words. Nothing is sent to your server until you say them, the recording starts after the phrase (nothing from before it is kept), and the audio is never stored: your server turns it into text in memory and drops it. Hey Sara is off until you switch it on, on each device, from that device.

She reads them and suggests what she learned; you check every line, and only what you keep is saved. Each companion has her own import: open it while talking to the companion it's for. Where: Settings → Privacy & system → Move in and export → Bring her from another app.

App What to upload How it's read ChatGPT The.zip from the data export (or conversations.json alone) The shown branch of each conversation; system prompts, tool output and hidden reasoning left out (the same reader as Bring your history) Claude The.zip from the data export (or conversations.json) Text blocks only; thinking and tool blocks left out Character.AI The account export.zip, or a chat.json Chats as turns with candidates (the chosen reply only, swipes left out), and the older histories…

The facts and summaries you saved become memory notes, labelled as learned from your imported history ("from your Character.AI chats"), dated when they happened. Kept chats are archived import-<app> conversations: the other app's lines are marked as theirs, never hers; they're left out of other apps, MCP and the API, like…

Sara runs on one server (Linux, Windows 10/11 or macOS 13+) for one owner. You need about 1 GB of disk for Sara itself, more for optional local voice (1.3 GB) and subscription programs (0.5 GB). A GPU is only needed if you want to run models locally with Ollama. How big a machine you need: REQUIREMENTS.md. Which model to pick: CHOOSING_A_MODEL.md. New to this? entries.t: More than one person on one server (optional)
entries.x: Since 2.0 the owner can invite other adults (a partner, a flatmate, a grown-up child) to use the same server, each with their own companions and a private space the owner can't read: Settings → Household → People on this server. Nothing to install; the owner chooses which models each person may use and a daily limit. Not on the demo server. See HOUSEHOLD.md. For complete separation (each with their own owner and server settings), use several Saras instead, below.

For a family, a small team or a hosting provider: several separate Saras on one Linux server, each with her own owner, data, settings, port, service and admin command. Nothing is shared between them except the server itself (and, if you use them, Tailscale, Caddy, local voice and the subscription programs). Native install: sudo sara update, or Settings → Privacy & system → Updates. Every update: makes a backup (in /var/lib/sara/backups), gets the new version and reinstalls it (your data and sara.env are not touched), restarts her and checks that she answers, puts the previous version back by itself if she doesn't. entries.t: Reading other people's text in six languages (U3.12)
entries.x: Sara reads promises in your sent mail and chats (S4), clause checklists and contracts (S7, E6) and booking mails (S6) in English, Spanish, French, German, Brazilian Portuguese and Italian. No model is used: each language has its own phrase set.
entries.p: Reading other people's text in six languages (U3.12)

entries.x: Detect, then read with one language only. src/lang-text.ts detectLang scores small words ("el/los", "le/vous", "der/und", "você/não", "il/della") and letters only one language uses (ñ, ß, ã, ò). English wins ties and empty text. A text is then read with its language's phrases only, never a mix: an English promise "I will book Mañana Café for the Freitag concert" gets no due day from the Spanish or German words, and an English contract never matches "Haftungsbegrenzung". entries.x: Library → Learn a language… is a few minutes a day of practice in Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian or English. Everything you hear and say stays on this computer: her local voice for that language speaks, and the local hearing on this computer listens. No cloud voice or cloud hearing is ever used here.

I'm learning: the language you practice. Meanings are shown in the language Sara uses for you (learning English in English shows Spanish meanings). My level: Beginner (A1), Elementary (A2) or Intermediate (B1). It picks the sentences and keeps her replies at that level in Talk practice. Cards a day: 5, 10 or 20 cards per session at most. Each language and level gets its own study set ("español · A1"), made from a built-in bank of everyday sentences. It is a normal Study set: it shows in Libra…

Cards: the sentence, then Show meaning and Again / Hard / Good / Easy. Spaced repetition (SM-2, the Study engine) brings hard cards back sooner. Listen: Play (or Slower) says a sentence in her local voice for the language; Show the words shows it with its meaning. Say it back: Hear it, then Say it and speak. With the multilingual hearing installed you see your words while you speak. Each word is marked right, close (with what she heard) or not heard, and you get one gentle tip ("Very close. L…

Practice talking opens Talk with Sara in a chat called "Practice: español" (one per language). In that chat she answers only in the language you learn, in one or two short sentences at your level, asks a question back, and adds at most one gentle correction ("You could say: …"). Talk hears you in that language and speaks with the local voice for it. Typed messages in that chat get the same treatment.

entries.t: What you need on this computer
entries.x: A local voice for the language (Settings → Voice; Piper voices are named by language). Local hearing in the language: English uses the normal local hearing; Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and Italian need the multilingual hearing (sara voice install --languages, W0.3). Without them the page says so plainly: cards always work, listening needs the voice, Say it back and Talk practice need both. A household member whose voice is turned off gets cards and progress only.

State per person: <dataDir>/lang-learn.json (prefs, practice days, words said right, the practice chat per language). Cards live in the person's own study tables. Routes ride the study family: GET|PUT /api/study/lang, POST /api/study/lang/say|hear|score|talk|warm. POST /api/voice/speak {local: true} is the Talk-practice voice: local only, 409 when the language has no local voice. Code: src/lang-learn.ts (bank, scoring, engine), src/lang-learn-note.ts (state file and her practice-chat note, re…

Point Sara at a topic or a website and she studies it for you: she reads public pages, keeps what she learned as a knowledge skill with its sources and the date she read them, can keep it fresh on a schedule, and answers your questions from it, citing the pages. Good for things that move: a launch you follow, a team, prices, a product's docs, rules that change.

In a chat: /learn heat pump rebates or /learn https://docs.example.com. Add quick, standard or deep, and daily, weekly or monthly to keep it fresh: /learn the Artemis program weekly. /learn alone lists what she has learned. Or just ask in the app: "learn about the Artemis program", "keep up with heat pump rebates". From a research run (3.1.2): when a research run is done, Save as a skill (or Keep it fresh, refreshed every week) learns from the pages that run read, without reading them again. …

A topic: a few web searches (she plans them), then she reads the best pages: about 5 (quick), 12 (standard) or 25 (deep). A website: only that site. She reads robots.txt first and skips what it disallows, follows links on the same site only, reads one page at a time with a pause between pages, and stops at the page cap: about 10, 40 or 80 pages. She never reads private or local addresses (your router, localhost, your network). Sturdier runs (3.1.2): a page that times out or answers 429/5xx is…

When a question is about a topic she learned, she loads those notes for that reply, answers from them, links the pages, and says how recent they are. If the last refresh failed she tells you it may be out of date. If your question goes beyond what she read, she says so and offers to look it up. A question counts as "about" a topic only when it shares a real topic word with it ("warcraft", "talent", "heat pumps"). Everyday words ("said", "two", "see", "need", in any of the six languages) never…

Pick Every day, Every week or Every month (or Refresh now). Each refresh reads again, keeps the previous notes as an older version (Settings → Skills → the skill → versions), and writes What changed since <date>: new facts and facts no longer in the sources. With Tell me when something changes on, she sends one message after a refresh that found something, never during quiet hours (it waits until they end). A refresh that fails marks the topic Out of date and keeps the last good notes; she tr…

Budgets: each run has a token cap by depth, and Settings → Budgets → Learning a topic sets a monthly learning budget (estimated tokens). When it is used up, new topics and refreshes wait. Content: the same rules as her chats: sexual content involving minors is always refused, and explicit topics need Adult mode. Admin policy: "learning": false (Settings → Policy → Turn off Learn a topic) stops new topics and refreshes on the server; what she already learned stays as skills. Audit: starting, c…
Sara turns something you want to learn into a study set and helps you keep it: flashcards, quizzes, a summary sheet and spaced repetition, all on your own server.

Make a set. Library → Study… → Make a study set: pick a Library document (and, for a long one, a chapter) or paste text, then Make cards. Or ask in chat: "make flashcards from chapter 3 of my biology book", "quiz me on these notes". What you get. Flashcards (front/back), fill-in-the-blank (cloze) cards, multiple-choice questions, short-answer questions with a rubric, and a summary sheet of the key points. Study. Study now (or a set's Study) shows one card at a time. Flashcards: Show the answe…

Settings → You → Briefing and reminders → Study cards: Setting What it does Remind me when study cards are due One reminder a day, only on days with cards due (on by default). Time When the reminder arrives (4:00 PM by default). New cards a day How many never-seen cards come up each day (20). Cards per new set The most cards one new set gets (5–60, default 20): the generation cost cap.

For a child in the household (Settings → Household, kid mode): Cards and feedback use words for their age group. Hints before answers: Show a hint comes first; the answer only after that. A wrong answer gets a hint and "want to try again?" instead of the answer. Homework is coached, never done (the same rule as "Make it sound human"): when the text is a worksheet or an assignment, the cards hold guiding questions and first steps, never the answers, and there is no summary sheet. Parent view: …

Everything is stored in your own space (a household member's sets live in theirs; nobody else sees them). In private local mode no reminder is pushed. Making a set costs one model call on at most about 24,000 characters of text; a short answer costs one small call. Any model works, local ones too. If the model's reply is not usable (small local models), Sara makes the cards herself from the text (fill-in-the-blank and multiple-choice cards plus a summary of the first sentences), so a set is a…

Name one person you trust and choose what they get if you stop using Sara: a letter, short notes, documents from your Library, sealed notes (for example a password manager hint), your details card and, only if you pick them, chats. Nothing is shared while you use Sara. Where: Settings → Privacy & system → Privacy → Legacy and emergency access. Design notes: design/LEGACY.md.

Set it up. Turn on legacy access, type their name, pick what they get, press Save and confirm it's you (passkey, two-step code or owner token). Sara shows their link once: give it to them on paper or in a message only they read. Before the page opens, the link shows only "closed for now" and nothing about you. Sara watches for you. Signing in, chatting with her (a message you typed: not automations, other apps or household members) or pressing I'm here counts as "you are here". Background app…
If you allow it, their page has an Ask for access button. You are told at once, and the page still waits the full waiting period, so you can cancel by signing in. One request per week.

Their link is 32 random bytes; Sara keeps only a fingerprint of it (and a vault-sealed copy for the opening email). Make a new link stops the old one. Wrong links are counted: after 20 misses from one address the page answers "too many requests". Documents download only while the page is open and only the ones you picked. Chats are not included unless you pick them; picked chats are shown with keys, passwords and email addresses blanked out. Sealed notes are stored encrypted in Sara's vault a…

Give her documents to keep (PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, EPUB e-books, web pages, Markdown, text and CSV files, photos of pages). She reads each one, remembers the key points (each with the exact words they came from), finds things in them by their words and by meaning, and says where an answer came from. Everything stays on your server. This page covers how it works, with the details of big documents (Phase 74, release 2.3). The short version for everyday use is in the in-app guide (Help →…

Library in the sidebar → Add documents (or drop files there), or 📎 in a chat (Keep in her library or Just read this once), or send the file to her on Telegram or Discord. How big: PDFs up to the owner's limit (Settings → Skills & tools → Library → Largest document, default 1 GB; choices 100 MB to 2 GB). Every other kind of file is read whole in memory and stays at 100 MB; save a bigger one as a PDF. Files sent through Telegram or Discord stay at 100 MB too (the bridges download into memory).…

A file is never held in memory on the way in: One request (POST /api/library?name=…): the body is piped to a temporary file in <data>/library/incoming/, stopped at the size limit. Resumable pieces (the app uses these for files over 8 MB): POST /api/library/uploads {name, size, keep, learn, conversation?} → {id, received: 0, chunkBytes} (refused with 413 before any byte if size is over the limit, 507 if the disk is too full); PUT /api/library/uploads/<id>?offset=N with up to 16 MB of the file …

PDFs are read page by page, from the file on disk, in a background job that keeps its state in the database (library_jobs), so it can be paused, cancelled, and carries on after a restart from the page it reached (anything stored past the last finished page is dropped first, so no page is stored twice). The Library shows the progress: Reading page 412 of 980 · about 6 minutes left, with Pause, Resume and Cancel reading (she stops; what she read so far stays searchable, with a note saying where…

Every scanned page is read (the old limit of 40 is gone). Settings → Skills & tools → Library → Scanned pages: Read them; ask me first when a cloud model would (default): with a picture model on this computer she starts by herself. With a cloud model she first shows how many scanned pages there are, which model would read them, about how long it takes and about what it costs (from the price table in Usage and costs; "not known" when the model has no price), and waits for Read them with this m…

Word search: SQLite FTS5 over every passage (about 1,400 characters, never across pages). Meaning search: vectors are stored exactly (Float32) in SQLite and searched in memory as 8-bit numbers (int8 with a scale per vector, a quarter of the size): a brute-force pass over the whole block finds the best 48, which are then scored again exactly. New vectors join the block as they are made. Measured at 100,000 and 300,000 passages in RESULTS.md. Both are merged by rank, and each passage she is giv…

Open a text or Markdown document she keeps and press Read together. It opens above your chat. Share this passage: select some text (up to about a page: 4,000 characters over at most 3 passages) and press it. Your next message comes with that passage; she comments on that text only. Follow my place (off by default,? tip): the passage at the top of the view is sent after 1.5 s still, at most once every 5 s (the server allows 12 a minute). Moving never starts a reply. Stop ends sharing at once (…

In the Library press Read a feed together (or use the Feed tab of an open Read together view). Paste the address of a public RSS or Atom feed (a blog, a news site, a podcast's show notes) and press Open. Sara's server fetches that one feed once, only when you press Open or Reload: never in the background, never while she writes a reply. Nothing is remembered: not the address, not the items (closing the view, Stop or a restart drops them). The list shows each item's title, date and site as pla…

Research a question… in the Library window plans web searches with you, reads public pages and writes a report where every sentence links a page she read; the report is kept here and downloads as PDF or Word. See Research a question. Documents she makes for you (Word, PDF, Excel, PowerPoint and more) are saved here too; see Documents she makes.

What she has learned… lists the topics and websites she studied for you (/learn, "learn about X"), with their status, what changed at the last refresh and the notes she keeps, with sources. See Learn a topic.

Meetings… in the Library window listens in a meeting room you start (everyone is told first) or reads a recorded meeting, and writes notes with a summary, decisions and action items; the notes are kept here and action items go to the Planner when you add them. See Meetings.

Library → Scan pages… turns paper into a Library document in one go: a letter, an insurance card, a whole contract. Press Use the camera (the phone app, a phone browser over https, or a webcam) and Take page for each page, then Done. Or press Add photos to pick pictures you already took (on a phone this also offers the camera). Each page is cut to the paper's edges and turned straight (switch Crop and straighten automatically off to keep whole photos). Tap a page to drag its four corners, or …

Library → Journal… keeps a short daily entry, just for you. Pick how today was (optional): Great, Good, Okay, Low or Rough day. Press Record a minute and talk; press Stop and save (it stops by itself at one minute). Or type it in the box and press Save entry. Only the words are kept. Tick Keep the recording to keep the audio too, so you can play it back. On this day shows what you wrote on this day in earlier years (or last month). Your words are heard by the hearing engine on this computer o…

What Where Originals <data>/library/<sha>.<ext> (uploads in progress in <data>/library/incoming/) Documents, passages, FTS, vectors library_docs, library_passages (with page), library_fts, library_vectors in her database Reading jobs, scanned pages, contents library_jobs, library_ocr, library_sections Code src/library/source.ts (reading a file in pieces), pdf.ts (the reader: cross-reference tables and streams read from the end, objects by offset, object streams; a scan of the file only when t…

EPUB and Word books get passages and key points but no contents or section summaries yet (the structure phase is for paged documents). Measured on the development PC only; the "small server" numbers are this PC with a 256 MB reader limit and the gentle speed (see RESULTS.md), not a real small server.
She can put a small checklist, table or chart right in the chat that keeps itself up to date: a packing list you tick off, this week's to-dos, the numbers one of your kept apps saves.

"Make me a packing checklist for Lisbon." A checklist you can tick appears in the chat. "Show my Home to-dos as a checklist." It lists the open Planner to-dos of that project. Tick one and the task is done in the Planner; finish a task anywhere else and it shows ticked here within a few seconds. "A chart of my runs" (or "a table of …") when one of your My apps saves the numbers: whatever the app saves next shows up in the chart. To change one she made with her own data, just tell her ("add su…
Library → My apps… → Live views in chats lists every live view, where its data comes from, Open the chat and Remove. Removing one stops it in every chat at once.

entries.t: What a live view can and can't do
entries.x: It runs in a sandbox, like My apps: it never gets your Sara sign-in, can't read the chat page, Sara's data or storage, and can't reach the internet. It can only read its own list, tick its own rows, and (for a small page she wrote) save its own data. A list over Planner to-dos can only tick the to-dos it shows. Each household member's live views stay in their own space. Details for developers: design, threat model.

entries.t: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else
entries.x: This guide is for someone setting up the Sara app on a Mac when Sara herself already runs on another computer or a server (for example sara.example.com). The Mac only gets the app; her memories, chats and settings stay on the server. Takes about five minutes.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: A Mac with macOS 13 (Ventura) or newer, Apple silicon or Intel. The address of the Sara server: the same address you open in a web browser to reach her (for example sara.example.com, or http://100.x.y.z:7860 on a Tailscale or home network). Someone already signed in to that Sara (in a browser, on a phone or another computer): they make a one-time sign-in code for the Mac. If that's you, have that device at hand.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: Open the latest release: <https://github.com/farena-ai/sara/releases/latest>. Under Assets, download Sara-<version>.dmg (about 110 MB). Or, if the server's owner put the app on the server: in a browser on the Mac, signed in to Sara, Settings → Connections → Devices and sign-in → Download for Mac. Or with Homebrew: brew install --cask farena-ai/tap/sara.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: Open the downloaded.dmg (double-click it in Downloads). Drag Sara onto the Applications folder in the window that opens. Eject the disk image (the ⏏ next to "Sara" in the Finder sidebar) and delete the.dmg if you like. The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any downloaded app. If macOS still asks "Sara is an app downloaded from the Internet. Are you sure you want to open it?", choose Open.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: Open Sara from Applications (or Launchpad, or Spotlight: ⌘Space, type Sara). The first screen asks how to use it. Choose Connect to a Sara somewhere else. Don't choose Run Sara on this Mac: that installs a new, empty Sara on this Mac. On Connect to your Sara, type the server's address in Address and press Continue. Plain names like sara.example.com use HTTPS automatically. Home-network and Tailscale addresses (192.168.…, 100.…, something.local) use HTTP. You can also type the full address wit…
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: The app now opens that Sara's sign in with a code page (a Code box). On the device that is already signed in, open Settings → Connections → Devices and sign-in and press Add a phone or computer. It shows a QR code and a short code like ABCD-EFGH-JKLM. The code works once and for 10 minutes. On the Mac, type the code in the Code box and confirm. If this is the first time on this device, Sara shows her short notice that she is an AI. Read it and continue. You're in: every conversation, her look…
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: macOS asks the first time each is needed. Allow them for the best experience; you can change them later in System Settings → Privacy & Security and Notifications. Notifications: messages, reminders and approvals while the window isn't in front. Approvals have Allow / Deny buttons; reminders have Done / Snooze. Microphone: for calls and voice messages. Camera: only for video calls, if you turn it on.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: The menu bar icon (top right, her picture) keeps Sara running when you close the window: Open Sara, Ask Sara…, what she's doing now, Settings…, Your Saras ▸, Open at login, Help, Quit Sara. Quitting the app doesn't stop the server; she keeps running there. Quick ask: press ⌥⇧S (Option-Shift-S) anywhere to ask her something in a small window. Change the shortcut in the menu bar icon → Quick ask shortcut, or in Sara's Settings → This computer. Files: drop files on the Sara icon in the Dock, or …
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.t: 7. More than one Sara, or moving to a different one
entries.x: Menu bar icon → Your Saras ▸ → Add a Sara… adds another server (each keeps its own sign-in; ✓ marks the one in use). Your Saras ▸ → Remove … signs out of one and removes it from the list.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: Update: download the new.dmg and drag Sara to Applications again (replace). Homebrew: brew upgrade --cask sara. Your sign-in stays. Remove: quit Sara (menu bar icon → Quit Sara) and drag Sara from Applications to the Trash. Nothing on the server changes. Also sign the Mac out on the server: Settings → Devices and sign-in → remove it, so its old sign-in can't be used again.
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.x: What you see What to do Can't reach your Sara Open the same address in Safari on the Mac. If Safari can't either, it's the network or the server; the app tries again every 30 seconds. The code is refused Codes work once and for 10 minutes: make a new one. Type it with or without the dashes. No notifications System Settings → Notifications → Sara → Allow notifications. Also check Focus / Do Not Disturb. The shortcut does nothing Another app may use ⌥⇧S: pick another in the menu bar icon → Quic…
entries.p: Install Sara on a Mac for a Sara that runs somewhere else

entries.t: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together
entries.x: Many people have more than one mailbox: a personal Gmail, a work Gmail or Google Workspace, an Outlook, an iCloud. Sara reads them all together. This page explains how; the basics of adding each kind are in EMAIL.md (Outlook, IMAP providers) and GMAIL.md (the Google sign-in).
entries.p: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together

entries.x: Settings → Connections → Apps and services → Email and calendar and Gmail and Calendar show the same list: every account with what it is used for (Mail ✓, Calendar ✓, Docs ✓), and one button, + Add an account, with every kind behind it: Google account: Google sign-in through your own Google app (set up once on the Gmail and Calendar page; without it this choice opens those steps). Google shows its account picker; pick the account to add and allow Sara. Each Google account has its own sign-in …
entries.p: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together

entries.x: Google: each Google account's main calendar shows; under Calendars you can tick others (shared or family calendars) or untick an account entirely. Outlook / Microsoft 365: the account's main calendar (on or off). iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo: press Turn on calendar on the account. The same app password opens the provider's calendar (CalDAV); every calendar with events is listed and can be ticked. For other providers Sara asks for the calendar (CalDAV) address from your provider's help pages. Gmail…
entries.p: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together

entries.x: Today's Mail card, searches ("find the email about the lease") and "what's waiting for my answer?" cover every mailbox by default. Each email is labeled with its mailbox. Under Combined inbox and Today you can leave a mailbox out (it is still there when you name it: "search my Yahoo for…"). The inbox helper has its own choice of mailboxes (Inbox helper section on the same page).
entries.p: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together

entries.t: Which address a reply goes from
entries.x: A reply goes from the mailbox that received the email. A new email goes from your default mailbox, unless you name another ("from my work address") or only another mailbox has written with that person before; then that one. The approval card shows From: before anything is sent.
entries.p: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together

entries.x: Each person's accounts are their own: a household member's mailboxes live in their own vault and never mix with the owner's. Google sign-ins are the owner's (members add Gmail with an app password). Addresses are shown on cards; tokens and app passwords stay encrypted in the vault and are never shown. The combined-view choices are kept in mail-view.json in your data folder (no secrets). Several companions (T62). The first companion uses every connected account. Any other companion uses none u…
entries.p: Several accounts: every mailbox and calendar together

entries.t: Shared by friends: the community marketplace (U4.27)
entries.x: People in a Messages community, or two linked friends, share useful things with each other: skills, prompt or workflow templates, automations, team recipes and links to Sara Store add-ons. Each Sara checks every item itself before anything is installed, shows exactly what installing does, and asks. Where: Settings → Skills & tools → Get more → Shared by friends (owner only).
entries.p: Shared by friends: the community marketplace (U4.27)

entries.x: Kind What crosses What installing does Skill the SKILL.md text only (name, description, steps); never its files adds the skill on trial (she uses it only for a strong match; switch it off in Skills) Template a prompt or workflow in plain words adds it as a skill on trial Automation its definition (name, when, steps) adds it paused; nothing runs until you turn it on Team recipe its plan (helpers, steps, delivery), through the team-recipe importer adds the recipe; a team run still shows its pla…
entries.p: Shared by friends: the community marketplace (U4.27)

entries.t: Checks (on the receiving server, before every install)
entries.x: Content hash: recomputed here over everything shown (id, kind, text, version, author, permissions, payload); a mismatch refuses the item. Install sends the hash you reviewed: if the item changed since, it asks you to review it again. No secrets: the redactor's key-shaped patterns and name = value secrets anywhere in the item. No hard-limit tools: the team-run hard limits (commands, sign-ins, settings, deletes…) plus the computer, mail sending, the vault and skill saving; tools that run comman…
entries.p: Shared by friends: the community marketplace (U4.27)

entries.x: Share again with a new version number to update. Everyone who installed it gets a notice; nothing changes until they review and install the new version (skills start on trial again, automations stay paused). Stars (1-5) and a short comment, one per server per item. Report: the community's owner (or, on a friend shelf, the friend who shares) sees the report and can remove the listing. Authors can withdraw their own.
entries.p: Shared by friends: the community marketplace (U4.27)

entries.t: Privacy and who can use it
entries.x: Owner only: household members, kid spaces and the demo have no Messenger, so no marketplace (403). Private local mode: nothing is fetched from or sent to other servers; the peer endpoint refuses. Only server names, item text, ratings and reports travel; comments and reports pass the redactor.
entries.p: Shared by friends: the community marketplace (U4.27)

entries.x: Talk to her in Element (or any Matrix app) through a Matrix account of her own, for example @sara-frank:matrix.org. It's free and takes about 15 minutes. There is no Sara account, relay or hub in between: the Matrix plugin talks to her homeserver directly, through connections Sara holds for it. The design is design/BRIDGES4.md §6–§7. Matrix comes with Sara as a plugin and stays off until you add it.

entries.t: Before you start: rooms with her are not end-to-end encrypted
entries.x: Sara can only read rooms with encryption off. Reading encrypted rooms needs a whole cryptography library (Olm/Megolm), which Sara doesn't have. So whoever runs the homeservers (matrix.org, or yours) can read your room with her. For private chats use Signal. The card asks you to tick I understand and want to continue first. Element makes new rooms and direct messages encrypted by default, and encryption can never be switched off later. That's why step 3 makes a fresh room with encryption off.
An email address for her new account (matrix.org asks for one). Your own Matrix account, in Element. About 15 minutes at a computer (Element's phone app may not let you switch encryption off).

Settings → Connections → Apps and services → Matrix, tick the box and press Start. It comes with Sara, so after Start there is one short step: what it can reach, and Add Matrix (the full plugin card is under Details; Sara proves it is her own plugin herself, and the files' fingerprint is checked as for every plugin). Each step turns ✓ only when Sara has checked it. Make her a Matrix account. Open app.element.io in a private browser window. Create account → server matrix.org (or Edit for your …

In your room: everything your other chats do: commands (/new, /model …, or with her name first: Sara new), typing while she works, a read receipt on your message, a progress message she edits as she goes (react ⏹ on it to stop her), then her answer as a new message. A message you send while she works steers her; she reacts 👀. Pictures and files go both ways; voice messages are heard when speech-to-text is set up. Encrypted rooms: she says once I can't read encrypted rooms yet… and leaves (or…

Switch on My homeserver runs on my network and type its address with the port in Her homeserver (for example 192.168.1.20:8008). Tailscale addresses work too when this computer is on Tailscale. Port 443 or 8448 means an encrypted connection; other ports are plain HTTP on your own network.

The card says it in one sentence with the fix: Couldn't find a Matrix server, Her server doesn't take passwords from apps (paste a token instead), Wrong Matrix ID or password, Her login ended (log her in again), That room is encrypted, She hasn't been invited yet, Her server asked her to slow down, That file is bigger than her server allows. Log her out on the card ends her login at her server (a real revoke) and removes the key from Sara.
With Nothing leaves this computer on, Matrix pauses (even a home server federates the room off this computer). Her server keeps your messages; she reads them when it's off.

Sara can listen to a meeting and write the notes: a summary, the decisions, the action items with who does them and by when, and the open questions. The notes are kept in her Library, each action item can become a to-do in your Planner when you press Add, and when the meeting matches an event in your calendar she drafts a follow-up email for each group of attendees that waits for you to press Send. Three ways in, all in the Library window under Meetings… (owner only; also #view=meetings and t…

Only you start a meeting. Household members, the demo and shared links can't. Starting a room needs the tick Everyone in the room knows Sara will listen and take notes. When it starts, the screen shows and Sara says out loud: "Hi everyone, I'm Sara, an AI. I'm listening and taking notes for this meeting." That notice is also the first line of the transcript. Another of your signed-in devices (a phone on the table, a tablet) can open the same meeting. It shows the same notice, and its micropho…

entries.t: Record this computer (Windows and Mac apps)
entries.x: In the Windows app, Meetings… → Record this computer records the default microphone (left channel) and everything the computer plays (right channel, Windows WASAPI loopback) as a 16 kHz stereo WAV in the app's data folder. Tick Everyone on the call knows it is recorded and agreed first. With Settings → Voice → Meetings → Remind me to tell everyone on (the default) the card shows the line to say ("I'm recording this call so my assistant can take notes. Is that OK?") and Sara says it out loud w…

Lines are named Speaker 1, Speaker 2 … and carry their time in the recording. A recording from the Windows or Mac app is split by channel: you (the microphone) are Speaker 1, everyone on the call (the computer's sound) is Speaker 2. Crosstalk goes to the louder side. Any other recording (an upload, one microphone) is split by voice when Better speaker separation is on (Settings → Voice → Meetings, on by default): a free add-on (about 40 MB, downloaded the first time a meeting needs it) makes …

Meetings are heard with the hearing engine on your Sara server whenever it's installed, even if chat uses a cloud speech service. A cloud engine (your Speech API or Grok voice) hears meetings only when Settings → Voice → Meetings → Let a cloud engine hear meetings is on; otherwise Meetings… says why it can't start. Private local mode still allows only the engine on this computer. Long recordings are cut into parts of about ten minutes in your browser (MP3, M4A, MP4 and WebM are turned into WA…

Each device listens hands-free like a call (it notices when someone starts and stops talking). What was said goes to your Sara server, is turned into text with your hearing engine (Settings → Voice → Speech to text) and shows up as a line, named by the device. If someone calls her by name ("Sara, what did we decide about the place?"), she answers in a sentence or two from what was said, and that device speaks it. She answers one thing at a time, at most 20 times in a meeting, and she doesn't …

Open a meeting and press Captions: big text that follows the meeting while it happens, newest line at the bottom. It works for a room (every device that joined sends what it hears; any other signed-in screen can show the captions without its microphone, for example a tablet on the table) and for a recording while she hears it, and it reads back a finished meeting the same way. Translate into puts a translated line under each caption, in one of 17 languages. The choice is the same setting as S…

Choose File, give it a name and tick the consent box. Recordings can be up to 3 hours in WAV, MP3, M4A, MP4, WebM or OGG; your browser sends them in parts of about ten minutes, and she hears each turn and names the speakers (see Who said what). She hears the whole recording, then writes the notes. The file's time tells her when the meeting was, for the calendar match.

One model call (the model picked for writing in Settings → Models & usage → Which model does what) writes the summary, decisions and action items from the transcript, only from what was said: an owner or date nobody named is shown as Not said. The notes are a document in her Library, Meeting notes - <name> - <date>.md, and stay there even when the meeting is deleted. Write the notes again asks again (for example after changing the model). The calendar event: when the recording's time (the Win…

What Kept The sound Not kept: heard and dropped. Tick Keep the recording to keep it with the meeting until you delete it (Download the recording). The transcript In her own database on your server, with the meeting, until you delete the meeting. Never sent to chat apps. The notes A document in her Library. Caption translations With the transcript in her own database (meeting_captions), one per line and language, until you delete the meeting. Audit rows meeting.start, meeting.join, meeting.fil…

Sara does not join Discord voice channels yet. Since March 2026 Discord requires every voice connection, bots included, to use its end-to-end encryption (DAVE, built on MLS) on top of its voice gateway, UDP transport encryption and Opus audio. Doing that well means either a large amount of cryptography code in Sara or native add-on libraries that would have to be built for every platform Sara runs on. Until that is decided, record the call (Discord's own clients, OBS or a recording bot you tr…

Stories she writes from your own life: My year 2026, or one trip, with picked photos, a narrated version, a PDF and, only if you ask, a share link. It lives in Your story (sidebar → More → Your story, Alt+Y), above Look back.

Open Your story. Under Memory lane, pick a story: a year that has something in it, or a trip. Press Write it. She writes in the background; you can close the window. On the story card: ✕ on a photo leaves it out of the story (and the PDF and any later share link). Narrate it records the story with the voice on this computer; then a player shows. Save as PDF downloads the story with its photos between the paragraphs. Share link… asks first, then makes a read-only copy that works for 7 days. St…

Source What is used Photo library (V4.1) Photos in the date range: date, place, the caption the local picture model wrote Our moments (Phase 70) Photos and kept moments from your chats (never adults-only ones) Journal (V2.9) Your entries in the range, word for word, and their mood Trips (S6) Trips from booking mail, and the photo library's made-for-you trip albums Your story (Phase 53) Milestones, promises, projects and scrapbook moments in the range Trips: a trip from your bookings wins over…

Only a model on this computer writes it (a loopback local model, the same rule as the photo library's picture model). Photos and journal words never go to a cloud model. With no local model, the story is put together in code from the same facts (places, dates, counts, captions); nothing is invented and the card says "Put together from your facts". Exact words: a quote that is not word for word in your journal or captions is dropped with its sentence (the Look back rule). Narration uses only t…

Off until you turn it on: Memory → Overnight tidy → Tidy her memory at night. Once a night, in your quiet hours (Settings → when she may message you), when nobody has written for half an hour, she tidies her notes about you. She never deletes anything. Design: ops/EC1213_DESIGN.md.

Merges duplicates. Two notes that say the same thing become one: the copy is marked as replaced by the kept note (pinned first, then the more used, then the older). Asks about notes that disagree ("Alex drinks coffee every day" and "Alex no longer drinks coffee"). Nothing changes until you answer on the card: Keep the newer, Keep the older or Keep both. entries.t: Moving Sara to a new server or computer
entries.x: Everything Sara knows lives in one data folder, and one backup file holds all of it: her conversations, memories, character, look, library, workspaces, settings and her keys. Moving her is: back up → install on the new machine → restore → switch off the old one. The backup format is the same on Linux, Docker, Windows and macOS, so you can also move between them (for example from a Windows PC to a Linux server).

Small web apps she builds for you (a plant-watering tracker, a packing list, a score keeper, a quiz for the kids) can be kept on your own Sara server, with every version and a little saved data.

In a chat, ask: "Make me an app to track watering my plants." She builds it. Try it, then say "keep it". She keeps it as version 1 (app_keep). Open the Library and press My apps…. Each app shows its version, size and how much it saved.

Editing after that builds on the version shown. Undo and older versions change the app's files only: what the app saved stays.

Open opens it in a new tab; Look here shows it inside the Library. Share a link makes a read-only address that works for an hour, a day, a week, a month or until you stop it. A companion pack is one file (name.sara-companion.zip) that holds a companion: her character, her personality dials, her look, her voice choice, her first message and a few starter skills. You can give one to a friend, keep one as a backup of how she was, or add one from the Sara Store (Settings → Skills & tools → Get more → Companions). A pack never holds anything about you or your life with her: no memories, no chats, no people you told her about, no keys, no vault, no pictures she sent you…

Open Settings → Sara → Companions and press Share her on her row. Tick what goes in. Her character is always in. Her personality dials are ticked too (with none set, she simply uses the defaults on the other side). Her look, closet, face reference, voice, first message and her own skills are your choice. The list shows each part's size. Routines she suggests: tap up to five routines from the gallery (they go in as { "id": … } entries). Nothing switches on for the new owner until they say so. …

You see her card first: who she is, what she can do, every line of her character (Read all of her), where she comes from and her licence. Add her always makes a new companion. Nobody you have now changes. If you already have a companion with that name, the card suggests another one. Up to 8 companions fit on one server. Her first chat star…

Dotted release numbers (for example, 2.69.0) do not make a pack explicit. Explicit prose and adults-only settings still need the Explicit rating; the safety and privacy checks always apply. While Adult mode is off for her, explicit lines in her character are held aside, adults-only closet looks are kept but never worn, and her intimacy works as Suggestive. When you turn Adult mode on for her (Settings → You → Adult mode, in a browser), ⋯ → Add the held lines puts them back.

A card's lorebook becomes at most 10 background lines, never memories; the card says how many were left out. A card's pictures stay on your computer: Sara never fetches a picture from a web address in a card. A card that describes a character under 18 with romance or sexual content is refused.

⋯ → Update from a file shows what changed, part by part: Parts only the author changed are ticked Take. Parts you changed and the author also changed are a conflict, ticked Yours. Her pronouns, her age and a higher rating are always your choice. Her name never changes. Her memories, your chats, people, Adult mode and everything you changed stay. ⋯ → Go back to the version before undoes the last update.

Nothing about minors, ever. A pack that gives an age under 18 with romance, or that describes a minor in a sexual way, is refused when it's made and again when it's added. There is no override. Her safety rules and the AI notice always apply, whatever the pack says. Lines like "never say you are an AI" are refused. A real person needs that person's written yes, and real-person packs never go on the Sara Store. If the Sara team pulls a store pack, she is paused: her chats stay readable, and ⋯ …

Memories stay the source of truth: correct a memory and the card's fact changes with it, forget it and the fact goes, and if a newer note replaces it the card shows it under Replaced by newer notes. entries.t: Two people with the same name
entries.x: If a name in your message matches several people, she decides in this order: A qualifier in the message wins: "Jeff from work", "my brother", a surname, an alias. Then context: who was just talked about in this conversation; a -work channel prefers work people; someone mentioned far more often recently. Otherwise she doesn't guess. She is told it could be either and asks you naturally when it matters. Your answer becomes an alias on the right card. Add aliases yourself on the card (Also called).

Photo or initials Who they are and circle (family, partner, friends, work, neighbours, other) Birthday (it shows on Today, once a year) What she knows, by date. Each fact has its source (your words; the link opens the message) and can be corrected, made private, or taken off the card. People linked to them ("Lea is Jeff's wife") Your own notes, which she reads but never rewrites Merge with…, Split… (move facts that are really about someone else to a new card) and Forget this person On a phone…

Your space only. Cards live in each household member's own space, per companion. Nobody else in the household sees your people, and there are no shared people. Private facts. Facts learned in a private conversation (or ones you mark) carry a lock. They are used only in private conversations. Sensitive facts are health, intimate, money and legal things about someone. They are: folded on the card until you open them; never on Today or in a notification; only brought up when you talk about that …

Mail they sent you and mail you sent them (headers of the mailboxes in your combined inbox), the chat rooms she keeps up with (Discord, Telegram groups), and calendar meetings (past and the next one). You can talk to Sara from your phone anywhere: same companion, same conversations. This page goes from nothing to a working phone, step by step.

A secure (HTTPS) address for your Sara. Phones need HTTPS for sign-in to stay private on the way, and browsers only allow notifications, the microphone and "Add to Home Screen" on HTTPS pages. You have two easy choices: Tailscale (recommended): a free app that makes a private network of your own devices. Sara gets an address like https://my-server.tail1234.ts.net that only your own devices can open, from anywhere, with nothing to open on your router. Install Tailscale on the server and on you…

With no signal (or while her server restarts), the app shows the recent chats and notes it kept, read-only, and keeps what you write as Waiting to send bubbles (edit or delete them) until it can send them, once each. On by default in the phone app; in a phone browser turn on Keep a copy on this device for offline in Settings → Connections → Devices and sign-in (an installed web app has it on). Needs an https address (Tailscale or your own domain). See OFFLINE.md.

Phone settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant app → Default digital assistant app → Sara. Then a long press on the home button (or the assistant gesture or key) opens her ready to listen (with voice set up) or with the cursor in the message box. "Hey Google" can't be replaced by another app, so it opens by press or gesture, not by voice. VOICE_ASSISTANTS.md

The iPhone app isn't in the App Store. Add Sara to the Home Screen from Safari for notifications and the badge, and use Apple Shortcuts for the share sheet, Siri and a widget: Settings → Connections → iPhone Shortcuts. IPHONE.md
A tile with today's reminders, what waits on you and Talk. Pair it with the code the watch shows: Settings → Connections → Phone and notifications → Wear OS watch. WEAR.md

entries.x: The Media Stream carries 8 kHz G.711 μ-law in 20 ms frames. Sara converts it to 16 kHz WAV for her hearing and her voice back to μ-law (src/phone-audio.ts). Speech turns are found by loudness (0.7 s of quiet ends a turn); talking over her clears what she was still saying. She hangs up after about 15 s of silence.

entries.x: src/telephony.ts is the adapter interface: verify a webhook, answer with a media stream, reject, place, hang up, record, and the stream's messages. A SIP trunk or WebRTC gateway (a PBX, a SIP provider's media API) would be a second implementation of the same interface; it is not built in, and choosing "SIP or WebRTC" says so.

entries.x: Joining a channel is one gateway message (op 4, Voice State Update) on the existing bridge connection, but the audio needs Discord's voice transport (a second WebSocket, UDP, encryption and the Opus codec). entries.t: Nothing leaves this computer (private local mode)
entries.x: Sara can run entirely on one computer: her server, her model and everything she knows. With the switch Nothing leaves this computer on, she doesn't connect to anything except that computer. This page says what the switch guarantees, how it's enforced, and what it can't promise. Where: Settings → Models & usage → On this computer. The same page helps you get a model that runs there. While the switch is on, a 🔒 Only this computer badge sits in the top bar.

A shared scene is one story you play with your companion across several of your own chats: your web chat and your own Telegram or Discord DMs, plus at most one shared room with other people (a Discord channel, a Telegram group or a DM with a guest). You give it a title, a premise and a few short canon facts ("the inn burned down"). Each linked chat sees the current canon in her replies, so the story carries from the web to your DM and into the room. Messages themselves are never copied betwee…

Settings → Connections → Pick up across apps → Session continuity → Shared scenes. Use shared scenes in linked chats (on by default). Off stops every scene from reaching her replies; every scene is kept and you can still open, unlink, reset or delete them. New scene: title (1–80 characters) and premise (up to 1500). The Adult scene box is shown only while Adult mode is on. Open scene: status (Active/Paused), linked chats, canon, and a Danger fold with Reset and Delete.

Pick one of your eligible chats; the card says who will experience the scene ("Only you, in your web chat.") and nothing happens until you press Confirm link. Eligible: your own open web chat, your own Telegram or Discord DM, or a plugin chat that is yours. Never: private (local-only) chats, coding chats, archived or ended sessions, group chats, work channels, voice assistants, apps/API/MCP/A2A/webhooks, or a chat with forgotten lines. A chat sits in one scene at a time; a scene holds up to t…

A scene can have one shared room: the room side of a Discord channel or Telegram group where she talks with other people, or a DM between her and one guest. A second room needs a second scene, so one group's words never reach another group. It must be a current room the bridge has recorded (its name and kind), its chat app must be on, and it must not be private, coding, archived, ended, a work channel, a voice room, a plugin chat or a multi-companion group chat. Your own lines in a channel st…

In a linked chat (yours, or the shared room) each line's menu has Add to scene, for you only. It shows the exact line, lets you pick an existing fact to replace or name a new one, and saves that line word for word as canon after the same safety checks (minors always; explicit text only in an adult scene). This is the only way a guest's words become canon. A line longer than 400 characters is refused (type the fact yourself instead). Editing, regenerating or forgetting the line, or removing it…

Canon facts have a short name (lower-case letters, digits and dashes, like inn or the-duel) and 1–400 characters of text. Changing a fact adds a version; the newest five are kept (History). Retire hides a fact (it stays in its history). Reset removes all canon and its history and keeps the title, premise and linked chats. Delete removes the whole scene. No message is ever changed. Limits: 20 scenes, 3 linked chats per scene, 40 current facts per scene. A limit is refused with a plain message;…

In a linked chat of your own she can keep the canon herself with the scene_canon tool: read: the title, premise, status, revision, who is in the scene and the current facts (at most 40 facts and 12000 characters; a fact that does not fit is left out whole and counted).
