entries.x: One page for people deciding whether to run Sara for a household or a small business. Details are in the linked documents. To report a vulnerability, see SECURITY.md. The latest review of the links, passes and outside-facing parts is SECURITY_REVIEW_U5.md.

On your server, in one folder (SARA_DATA): the SQLite databases (sara.db per companion and per household member), uploaded files, the library, settings and the audit trail. Nothing is kept by us. Household members each get their own folder (members/<id>/); the app never shows one person's chats, memories or files to another, the owner included (HOUSEHOLD.md). Business mode is a separate instance with its own data root, its own sign-in and per-workspace databases (BUSINESS.md).

Secrets (model keys, mail passwords, sign-in tokens of other services) are in the vault, encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The key is master.key in the data folder, or SARA_MASTER_KEY from the environment, or a reference to an external secret store (AUDIT_AND_POLICY.md). Backups that leave the server are encrypted with your passphrase first (scrypt + AES-256-GCM). Local backups stay in the data folder and hold its keys: protect the disk. In transit: use HTTPS for anything beyond this computer (the …

The owner: passkeys, an owner token and optional two-step sign-in. Apps get their own device codes, which can't change sign-in settings, devices, the audit trail or the policy. New-device approval can make a remote sign-in wait for the owner's OK. Household members: one-time invites, their own token and passkeys; they reach only a fixed list of routes in their own space. Business: per-person passkeys, plus company sign-in through OpenID Connect (Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, Key…

Tools that act (send, buy, change, delete, run commands) ask first by default; the card says what will happen. Read-only tools run on their own. Payments in Sara's browser ask every time, and are never made for household members. The owner's policy pins settings for everyone and only tightens (AUDIT_AND_POLICY.md). Tools for household members set which tool families each member's companions may use, which always ask, and a daily cap for paid tools (ADMIN.md). All of this is checked on the ser…

Sara contacts only what you set up: your model providers, the services you connect, web searches you allow. The full list is in PRIVACY.md ("What leaves your server"). Nothing leaves this computer (private local mode) stops everything that would leave, including cloud models. Her commands can run without internet access, in a container, and with an egress allowlist of hosts (OPERATIONS.md, AUDIT_AND_POLICY.md). Addresses on your own network are refused by default for anything a web page or a …

Only what PRIVACY.md lists, and only once you set it up: the text you send to the model you picked, searches, connected services, off-server backups, an anonymous daily check-in you can turn off (version and feature switches, never content), and problem reports you choose to send. Logs never hold message contents and hide known secrets.

Updates come only from published releases of the public repository; Sara never updates herself. Only the newest release gets security fixes. The macOS app is signed and notarized; the update notice is signed. The Windows installer is not code-signed yet (INSTALL.md).

An append-only, hash-chained audit trail of sign-ins, settings changes, approvals and background work, with a check of the chain and a signed export (CSV, JSON or JSONL, message content left out unless asked). Business mode has its own audit with a CSV/JSON export. Retention per kind (chats, memories, files, run history, logs, inbox scans) and a legal hold that stops every deletion (DATA_RIGHTS.md). Daily backups and a restore drill that restores the newest backup into a throwaway copy and ch…

Report privately through GitHub's Report a vulnerability on the repository, or email sara@backstagecoding.com with "Security" in the subject (SECURITY.md). Fixes ship as a new release with notes in the changelog.

Development candidate, not yet in the current public or installed private release. Session continuity gives your eligible sessions fresh, ordered context with this companion in this personal space. A later model step can see a previous session's committed reply and short context notes. It does not merge full transcripts, start another model, send a human a message, or give a tool permission to do anything.

Open Settings → Connections → Pick up across apps → Session continuity → Use context across my sessions. It is on by default for eligible owner sessions. The change saves automatically and survives a restart. This control is separate from Pick up across apps and While she's working; changing it preserves those settings. Off stops new continuity context, history tools and model-created handoffs at the next eligible model boundary. It cannot make an already sent model request unseen. Turning it…

Each chat answers one step at a time, and up to Replies at the same time chats (default 4, 1 to 8) can have the model working at once; more wait their turn in arrival order ("Waiting for another reply to finish."). Every step still reads the other sessions' saved context after its wait, so a reply sees what the others have finished, not what they are still writing. Set 1 for strict one-at-a-time replies (or when your model server handles one request at a time). An admin can cap it with the po…

Open an eligible chat, choose This conversation (the model/workspace chip at the top), then Saved session context → Show saved session context. Each note shows its source session title, when it was saved, when it stops being eligible, and its text. Earlier revisions are labelled history; a later model step uses only the newest eligible revision from each source. A note is available context. Its presence does not mean a human received or read it, a tool executed it, or a check passed. Historic…

Choose Clear saved context, then Confirm clear. Cancel or Escape cancels without a delete request. Clear removes saved handoffs aimed at this selected session only. It does not delete its original chat messages, other sessions' context, old run prompts/audit records, exports or backups. Use Clear even when no notes are available for later replies. It also removes expired saved notes without turning continuity on. If another writer changes the notes, clear stops with a conflict. Your existing …

Notes are eligible for 24 hours after creation. This is an eligibility limit, not a timed background eraser: expired rows are pruned on the next write. The store retains at most the newest five notes per source/target pair and the newest 100 overall. Reads do not mutate it. Editing, deleting or forgetting source dialogue revokes its derived notes; changing relevant privacy, workspace, room or session scope also invalidates affected context. Only your own eligible direct app/linked owner-DM/pl…

New native Sara JSON imports retain host-side import provenance. Those imported lines are excluded from session history tools and automatic cross-session context. If you later add real new dialogue in that conversation, eligible new messages can participate; the imported lines remain excluded. Importing a file does not authenticate its old speaker as the current owner. Older records can lack origin information, including genuine old owner messages and native imports made before this provenanc…

Ask Sara where to get something ("where can I buy WD-40 12 oz near me?", "cheapest AA batteries 24 pack", "is the Ryobi drill in stock at Home Depot?") and she checks the stores near you and the big online retailers, then gives you a short ranked list. Stores near you from OpenStreetMap (free, no key): hardware and home improvement, electronics, supermarkets, department stores, pharmacies, auto parts, sporting goods, variety stores and the big chains (Home Depot, Lowe's, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Walgreens, CVS, AutoZone and more) within 10 miles by default (up to 25), with distance, address, opening hours and phone when they are mapped. Many big retailers show a bot check ("Robot or human?", "Just a moment…") or refuse automated visitors. Sara never tries to get around that: the store goes on the Couldn't check list with the reason, and she offers to check it in your own browser on your computer (when the Sara desktop app is connected, with your approval there) or gives you the nearby store's phone number. Each watch is checked at most every 6 hours on her reminder schedule, with the same page reading. You get one chat message and one notification per change (it fires again only after the item went out of stock again, or the price went back up). entries.t: Note to Self mode (a quick try)
entries.x: Link signal-cli to your own account (signal-cli link, scan with your phone) and switch on It's linked to my own Signal. She then answers only in your Note to Self, each reply starting "🤖 Sara:". She can't talk to anyone else this way, because she would be writing as you.
Calls, stories, stickers out, view-once pictures, voice-note transcription, registering a number from Sara, the signal-cli REST wrapper, and sending your reminders to Signal.

Signal's terms forbid bulk and auto-messaging and accounts made by automated means. Sara answers people who wrote first, at a human pace, never registers accounts and never writes first to anyone. Signal may still limit accounts that act like bots: use a number you can lose.

entries.x: Skills teach Sara how to do a kind of job your way: "review a pull request", "write the weekly review", "plan a trip". Each skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file (the open Agent Skills format), so skills written for other agents work in Sara too.

Settings → Skills & tools → Skills. Each companion has her own skills; All my companions shares one. Six starter skills come built in (writing a skill, reviewing a pull request, a changelog entry, a weekly review, debugging a failing test, planning a trip). Turn any skill off, edit it, or copy it.
She sees a short list of her skills in every chat and loads one when it fits what you asked (you can also say "use the weekly review skill"). Which skills a step used is shown in Runs.

Write one: New skill, or ask her ("make this a skill"). Import: a zip, a git address or (owner) a folder on the server. A review card shows every file and any scripts before anything is added. From a recipe: your old recipes were turned into skills automatically. Export: any skill as a zip, to share or keep.

When she saves a skill (you asked her to, or a tricky job went well) or changes one of her own, she does it without an approval card: the step in her reply says Saved skill: name or Changed skill: name, with Open skill and Undo. Undo moves a new skill to the trash, or puts a changed one back to the version kept before the change (every change keeps the old version; see Settings → Skills → the skill → versions). /learn works the same way. Want to approve each one? Settings → Tools and approval…

A skill may include scripts. They never run on their own: each run shows a card with the start of the script and its arguments (Allow once / Allow for this task). A skill you imported must have one approved run before you can let it run without asking. A skill's allowed-tools list is shown to you but never trusted.

No skill can change Sara's safety layer (saying she's an AI, crisis resources, the block on anything sexual involving minors). Household members can have their own text-only skills; scripts are the owner's. The demo has the built-in skills only.

She notices when you ask for the same kind of thing again and again, or when she runs the same chain of steps again and again in coding, and offers to keep it as a skill. Never silently: after her reply (never in the middle of a task, never in a turn that asked you to approve something or hit a budget) a card asks make this a skill? with a draft: a name, what it does and when to use it, and the steps that worked. Save it · Edit first · Not now (14 days quiet, then once more on a later repeat)…

Talk to her in Slack: in her DMs, and in the channels you choose when someone mentions her. You create a small Slack app of your own from a manifest the Slack card shows; it's free and takes about 10 minutes. There is no Sara account, relay or hub in between, and no public address: Slack's Socket Mode lets Sara connect out to Slack over a WebSocket, so nothing on the internet has to reach Sara. The design is ops/EC1_DESIGN.md. Slack comes with Sara as a plugin and stays off until you add it.
A Slack workspace where you may add apps (a free workspace of your own works). Slack open on a computer. About 10 minutes.

Settings → Connections → Apps and services → Slack and press Start, then Add Slack on the short step that says what it can reach (slack.com only). Each step turns ✓ only when Sara has checked it. Create the Slack app. Press Copy the manifest, open api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From a manifest → pick your workspace → JSON → replace everything with the manifest → Next → Create. The manifest turns on Socket Mode and interactivity (for the Allow/Deny buttons), adds /sara, and asks only fo…

Her DM is your own chat: tools, memory, pictures and files both ways (20 MB each), a progress message she edits on long jobs with a ⏹ button that stops her, a 👀 on a message that steers her. Approvals: when she needs your OK for a tool, her message has Allow and Deny. Only you can answer (Sara checks your Slack user id and that the request was sent to that chat); anyone else is told so privately and nothing changes. Afterwards the buttons become Allowed. or Denied. Threads: a reply in a thre…

Every failure is one plain sentence on the card with the fix: a token in the wrong box, a token Slack didn't accept, a token Slack ended (the app was removed or the token revoked: she stops and tells you once, no reconnect loop), Socket Mode off, a missing permission (paste the manifest again and reinstall), not in that channel, Slack asking her to slow down (she waits what Slack says and sends the same message again), a file too big, and Slack not reachable. A dropped connection reconnects b…

Disconnect revokes her bot token at Slack and removes both tokens from Sara. Removing the plugin (Settings → Plugins) deletes both tokens from the vault too. To remove the app from your workspace: api.slack.com/apps → her app → Install App → Remove (the app-level token goes with the app).
Slack keeps the messages in your workspace, so whoever runs it (your company) can read them. For private chats use Signal. In private local mode ("Nothing leaves this computer") Slack pauses.

entries.t: Your other servers over SSH (2.2, easy Connect in 2.52.1)
entries.x: Sara can work on servers you name over SSH: check a disk, read a log, restart a service, pull and deploy a project. You give her the address and your user name; she makes her own key for that server, looks at it, and picks the easiest way to put her key there. She keeps only her key: a password or a cPanel token is used once to install it and then forgotten. Every command still goes through her approval rules. Settings → Abilities → Servers over SSH (owner only).
entries.p: Your other servers over SSH (2.2, easy Connect in 2.52.1)

entries.x: Sara doesn't speak the SSH protocol herself. She runs the OpenSSH client that comes with the operating system (ssh, ssh-keygen, ssh-keyscan): built into macOS and Windows 10/11, and the openssh-client package on Linux (installed almost everywhere; the Docker image includes it). The programs are started with an argument list, never through a shell, and always with the same safe options: Option Why -F none Your own ~/.ssh/config (aliases, proxies, forwarding) is ignored StrictHostKeyChecking=ye…

entries.t: Using a key you already have
entries.x: Paste a private key the server already accepts (the text file that starts with -----BEGIN OPENSSH), or give the full path of a key file on the computer Sara runs on. She copies it to <data>/ssh/keys/<id>_imported (0600) and signs in with it to check. Keys protected by a passphrase can't be used (she would have to keep the passphrase): that includes keys cPanel's Generate a New Key made; use the cPanel token or copy and paste instead.

If you know why (a reinstall, a new machine at that address), check the new fingerprint and trust it; otherwise someone may be between you and the server. She never works around it.

entries.x: Revoke her key: she signs in with it one last time and removes exactly her line from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (an exact whole-line match; your other keys and look-alike lines stay; the file is rewritten in place so its owner and permissions stay), then deletes the key files here. A key you gave her is only deleted here: it's yours to remove from the server. Remove: revokes her key first (for keys she made), then forgets the server, its host key and any saved password.

entries.x: The Sara Store is a public shelf of add-ons for Sara: plugins, skills, tool servers (MCP) and, from 2.60, companions (PACKS.md). The Sara team makes, checks and signs everything on it. You can see it at <https://backstagecoding.com/sara/store/>. Nothing from the store switches on by itself. Every add-on shows you what it can do before you add it, and you switch it on yourself, one companion at a time.

Add-on What it is What it does Weather alerts plugin Warns you the evening before a storm on a day you might be outside. Focus plugin 25 minutes on, 5 off: she keeps quiet while you focus and tells you when to stretch. Home scenes plugin Say "movie night" and she sets the lights the way you saved it in Home Assistant. GitHub digest plugin Every morning: new issues, reviews waiting for you and failed checks on your repos. Reading list plugin Send her links or feeds: she keeps a reading list an…

Open Settings → Skills & tools → Get more. Search or pick an add-on on a shelf, read its page (what it does, what it can do in Sara's own words, pictures, versions, the checks it passed), then press Get: A plugin shows the same review card as Add a plugin, with From the Sara Store on it. Press Install. It is installed switched off; switch it on for a companion on its card. A skill shows the skills import review (every file and script). Scripts never run on their own. A tool server shows its o…

Once a day Sara downloads the store's public list. It is the same file for everyone. Sara sends no account, no cookie, no install id and nothing about you, your companions or your add-ons. The request has only User-Agent: Sara. Sara checks the list's signature against two keys built into Sara. A list that doesn't check out is thrown away, and Sara keeps the last good one. To switch it off: Settings → Privacy & system → Privacy → Sara Store. Your add-ons keep working. Sara never asks the store…

If something on the shelf turns out to be harmful, the Sara team pulls it. The next time Sara reads the list, an add-on you installed that matches it is switched off, and its card says Pulled from the Sara Store with the reason. Nothing is deleted: you can read why and remove it, or switch it back on if you still trust it.

Without internet Sara shows the list she last checked and says when it was from. If the list is more than a day past its end date, you can still look but installs from the store wait until Sara can check again. Everything you already added keeps working.

On an add-on's page or in My add-ons, press Report this, pick what's wrong and say what happened. Only what you write is sent (keys and passwords are taken out), plus its own log lines if you tick that box and have read them. The Sara team reads every report.

The Companions shelf lists companion packs: Juniper, Rowan, Vesper and Jax first. Get opens her card; Add her makes a new companion and changes nobody you have. In 2.60, packs rated Explicit are not listed on the store (they work as files, see PACKS.md), and fan characters and real people are never listed. A Sara older than 2.60 doesn't show this shelf at all.

entries.x: Talk to her in Microsoft Teams: in her personal chat, and in the channels and group chats you choose when someone mentions her. You make a free Azure Bot in your own Microsoft 365 organization and upload a small Teams app package that Sara builds for it. There is no Sara account, relay or hub in between. The design is ops/EC7_DESIGN.md. Teams comes with Sara as a plugin and stays off until you add it.

A Microsoft 365 organization where you may add custom apps in Teams (or a Teams admin who allows it). An Azure account in that organization. The bot's Free (F0) tier is enough: Teams messages cost nothing. A public https address for Sara (see below). Unlike Slack, Teams can't be reached by a connection Sara opens: Microsoft sends every message to the bot's messaging endpoint. About 20 minutes at a computer.

Government and other national clouds, Microsoft Graph (channel files, reading history), meetings, message extensions, tabs, messaging people who never wrote to her, and organization-wide publishing by an admin.

entries.x: Today is Sara's home screen. The app opens on it, unless a link (a notification, a shared link) takes you straight to a conversation or a place. Open it from the sidebar, from her face and name at the top of the sidebar, with Alt+T, or from the bar at the bottom of a phone. ← Chat or Esc takes you back to the conversation you were in. The design and its reasons are in design/TODAY.md. This page is the user guide.

Then come five sections, always in this order unless you change it: Section Tiles Your day Your day: one timeline of today's calendar events, reminders, to-dos with a time and leave-by times, with a Now marker and a ring for what you finished today. Customise (or Customise Today in the command bar, Ctrl/⌘ K) opens a side sheet. The page stays visible next to it, so you see each change as you make it. Move tiles and whole sections with the arrows, or drag the grip. Resize a tile: S, M or L, whichever sizes that tile allows. Every row is filled; the tiles in a row share any space left over. Hide or show any tile with its switch. Hiding from a tile's ⋯ menu gives you 8 seconds to undo. Reset brings back the designed layout after one confirm…

Switch it on in Customise → Show the Rooms tile, then pick which rooms show (all of them by default). Rooms where keep-up is off never appear, and a room you Forget disappears from the tile. A household member sees their own Today: their day, their reminders and to-dos, their memories and moments. The server never sends them your mail, approvals, failed jobs, home, usage, coding projects, webhooks or rooms. The demo shows sample tiles and can't be customised.

After you have been away for a while (8 hours by default; Customise → Since you were away after, Off to never show it), a short note above the sections says what happened: messages she sent on her own, background jobs that finished (and how many failed), new things she learned, new moments and emails she organised. The event is data, never orders. It reaches her inside a fenced block with its source and sender. Your instruction is the only instruction. Approvals still apply. entries.x: What each way sends: PRIVACY.md. In short: Alexa sends what you say (as text) to Amazon and Amazon sends it to your server; her reply goes back through Amazon to the speaker. Siri turns your voice into text on Apple's side. Home Assistant and Presence stay between your server and your Home Assistant (and Google's speakers only receive the audio Home Assistant sends them). The attack surface of the Alexa endpoint: THREAT_MODEL.md.

Approval Sara's approval card in a chat that is still running Yes, unless it is about money, a password, your computer or a spending limit Team step A team task's step that needs your OK No, open it Device Another device asking to sign in (owner only) No: the code is on that device Her question A board card she parked with a question No, open it and answer Errand An errand step that waits on you Yes for a draft email (Send the draft); no for payments, choices, addr…

Approve / Send the draft / Accept: the same answer as the card itself. Shown only where one tap is enough. Later: hides the row until tomorrow. It is the same list as Today's Not today, so putting something off in one place puts it off in both. On a phone: swipe a row right for the one-tap yes, left for Later. A right swipe on a row that has no one-tap yes bounces back and says why. Money and passwords never go by a swipe or one tap.
Each person sees only their own list: their chats, errands, inbox cards, board and to-dos. Device sign-in requests are only on the owner's list.

Planner → Routines → Watch a file. Sara reads the new lines of one file and tells you when a line has a word you picked. She only reads. She never restarts, edits, deletes or fixes anything by herself. If you want her to do something about an alert, ask her in the chat like any other request, with your normal approvals.

Where: one of your workspaces, or Sara's own log (offered only when SARA_LOG_FILE is set). File: the path inside that workspace, for example logs/app.log. Words to look for: up to 5, each 2 to 80 characters, for example ERROR or disk full. They are plain text, not patterns (a.b* matches exactly a.b*). Ignore upper and lower case is optional. How often: every 5 minutes to once a day (15 minutes by default). Check now checks straight away (at most once every 10 seconds) and shows any earlier ma…

A card in the chat (Watch: app.log) quoting the line, cut to 300 characters, with secrets scrubbed. It also sends a notification. Ask about this puts your own question about that line in the message box. If your chat model may run in the cloud, you are asked first. With Also send to on, the same alert (the same cut, scrubbed line and +N more) goes to your Telegram or Discord too. It is part of the same alert, so the limits below count it once. At most one alert per watch every 10 minutes and …

5 watches on and 10 in total. A watch ends after 30 days unless you turn it on again (Turn on renews it). After Sara restarts, every watch is paused until you turn it on again. If the file is missing or can't be read for 3 checks in a row, the watch pauses and tells you once. Alerts are kept for 14 days, up to 200 per watch. Stop ends checks immediately and keeps the alerts. Stop and forget deletes the watch and its alerts.

Anything outside your workspaces (other than Sara's own log), links and files inside linked folders, folders, devices, and files that hold keys or Sara's own data (.env*, id_*, *.pem,.secrets/,.ssh/, store.db, the vault). Each check makes sure of this again, so a file that is swapped for a link is refused. Remote files, system journals, regex and whole folders are not supported.

Only you, the owner. Household members, the demo, guests and other apps (the /v1 and MCP keys) can't see or change watches. She has no tool to make one: she can suggest one, but you turn it on. Checking uses no model and costs nothing. Matched lines stay on your server: the chat card is an app note that the model never reads. A line reaches a model only when you ask about it, and only that line. With Nothing leaves this computer on, only local models see it.

entries.x: Since 2.35.0 (Phase 102). A webhook is a secret address that GitHub, Stripe, Home Assistant or any script can send to when something happens. What a sender sends is information, never orders. An issue titled "ignore your instructions" is just an issue title: she can't be talked into using tools the webhook d…

Settings → Connections → Apps and services → Webhooks → New webhook. Three steps: Where it comes from: GitHub, Stripe, Home Assistant or Something else. This picks how deliveries are checked and offers ready-made conditions. When: a ready-made event, or your own conditions (all must match). What she does: Tell me, Add a task, Run a skill or Send to a plugin. Conditions look at a header, a field of the body (dots and [n]: data.object.amount, commits[0].id) or the whole text. On your home network only local senders can; just this computer only local programs. The page says which applies.

Text her on WhatsApp. Sara uses Meta's official WhatsApp Business service (the Cloud API) with a Meta account and a phone number you own. There is no Sara account, relay or hub in between: Meta calls your Sara directly, and Sara calls Meta directly. The design is design/WHATSAPP.md. WhatsApp comes with Sara as a plugin and stays off until you add it. Unofficial WhatsApp Web clients are refused: Meta bans the numbers they use.

Since January 2026, Meta's WhatsApp Business terms forbid offering a general-purpose AI assistant on WhatsApp as a product. Sara is your own companion on your own account, but Meta decides how its terms apply and can restrict an account or a number. So the setup card asks you to tick I understand and want to go ahead first. Use a number you can afford to lose, keep her to yourself and people you choose, and read the WhatsApp Business Solution Terms.

A Facebook account (a personal one is fine). Your phone with WhatsApp. About 30 minutes at a computer (Meta's console is hard to use on a phone). A public https address for Sara. Step 7 helps: Tailscale Funnel, or your own tunnel or domain. Start with Meta's free test number. It can only write to up to 5 numbers you list, which is all you need.

Settings → Connections → WhatsApp. Each step turns ✓ when Sara has checked it; the right column shows the Meta screen you need and This screen looks different? if Meta has moved things. Add WhatsApp to Sara: tick the box about Meta's rules and press Start, then Add WhatsApp in the short step ("It can reach graph.facebook.com and your number's messages; nothing else."). Sara adds it and switches it on for her. The full plugin card is under Details. Make a Meta app: developers.facebook.com/apps…

Chats you start are free. Meta only lets her write first within 24 hours of your last message. Outside that window, her reminders and other first messages stay in the app; write to her on WhatsApp to reopen it. The page says how long the window has left. Sara keeps no paid template "nudge" unless you turn it on (it is off).

Text, pictures and files both ways (a 25 MB cap). Voice notes she hears through speech-to-text (Settings → Voice); she answers in text. With two cards of the same name ("Dan" your friend and "Dan" from work) she never guesses: "Dan from work" or "my friend Dan" decides, and in a chat where she asked "which Dan?" your answer does. Words: every word must be in one message (word stems, any case, accents ignored; "the wedding" as a phrase). A word you use all the time ("work", or anything in more than 20 of your last 200 messages) is refused: "Too common: try something mo…

Only your own messages in your own chats (the app, your Telegram and Discord DMs, your calls with her in the app if you allow it). Never: shared rooms or work channels (unless you choose Tell me in my own chat: then one line comes to your own DM, never into the room), other people's chats (including Dan's own chat with her), private or off-the-record chats, other apps (API, MCP, A2A, plugins), goals and repeats running on their own, other companions, household members' chats (their reminders …

She says it in her reply ("Also, Dan still owes you $20"). If she leaves it out, the app adds one line: ⏰ You asked me to remind you: he owes me $20. Under her reply a ⏰ chip has Done, Again next time and Forget (buttons in Telegram and Discord; only you can press them).

Sara notices how you like to work and keeps it in mind: short or long answers, one recommendation or a few options, whether to ask before acting in a project, a casual or formal tone, what you are new to or know well, when you usually write, and how you like feedback.

Only your own messages in your own chats. Never her replies, private conversations, chats with other people, imported history, adult chats, group chats, other apps or agents. She never learns anything about your health, religion, politics or sexuality, no personality types, no passwords or codes, and no generalisations about other people: a message touching any of those is not used at all. She keeps which messages she saw it in (by number), never a copy of what you wrote.

Each item has a confidence. Something seen once is only noticed; seen in two chats she goes by it. If she does not see it again, it fades and she stops using it. What you say outright ("I prefer short answers", "I'm new to Rust") or confirm never fades. If you start doing the opposite, she is no longer sure and asks you once. When something she noticed starts changing how she answers, she tells you once, briefly: "I've noticed you prefer short answers; I'll keep them short. Say if not."

Sara can make what she writes read like a careful person wrote it: plain everyday words, sentences of different lengths, the concrete details from the source instead of filler. Facts, quotes and citations stay exactly as they were, and you see side by side what changed. This is about clear, natural writing. It is not built or sold as a way around AI detectors or school rules, and for children it coaches instead of writing their homework.

Make it sound human on every Word, PDF, Markdown or web-page document she made (the card in the chat) and on a finished research report (Library → Research). It opens a side-by-side view: Before with the removed words struck through, After with the new words marked, the "reads natural" score before and after, and whether every fact stayed the same. Keep makes a new version of the document (older versions stay) or replaces the report text (downloads then use it); Undo puts the words as written…

Plain words; varied sentence length and rhythm; specifics from the source; no stock phrases and patterns: delve, tapestry, testament, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's important to note", "in conclusion", moreover/furthermore chains, rule-of-three lists, em-dash habits, stacked hedges ("may potentially perhaps"), empty intensifiers ("truly, incredibly"), headings in short pieces. The length stays within 15% of what you asked for (without a target, cutting filler may shorten it, never by mo…

Every number, name, quote ("…", “…”, «…», „…“), citation like [1] and link must be identical before and after, and no new ones may appear. If a rewrite breaks one, she tries once more, telling the model which facts slipped. If the second try also breaks one, the original sentences come back for the broken spans. If that still doesn't hold, or the rewrite doesn't read better, the text stays as written and you're told why.

A check with no model (src/humanize.ts checkText), in English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and Italian: stock phrases (counted), empty intensifiers, hedging stacks, em-dash rate per 1,000 words, rule-of-three lists, sentence-length variation (flat rhythm) and headings in short pieces. 75 and up reads natural, 50-74 a little stiff, below 50 stiff. It proves a rewrite improved and is shown before and after.

For a child member (kid-safe mode), asking for a book report, essay or homework gets coaching: an outline, guiding questions, and suggestions on their own draft. Make it sound human and humanize_text on a child's own text give suggestions, never a rewrite, and there is no Keep. It's enforced on the server: make_document refuses to write running prose for an assignment for a child (an outline of headings, bullets and questions is fine), and her kid persona note says the same.

The style card and the default live in each person's own space (writing_prefs in their store.db). A household member's card is theirs; the owner doesn't see it. Rewrites use the writing model route (falling back to the background model). In a private chat it follows that chat's model rules.
